To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
L2-nonexpansive networks can be trained to achieve state-of-the-art robustness against L2-bounded attacks and to generalize better from noisy data with random labels.

the proposed neural networks are well-conditioned in a sense that is both mathematically precise and practically useful, they are robust to adversarial attacks without needing any adversarial retraining, they generalize better from noisy data, and their outputs are meaningful.
a new regularization scheme and a new loss can improve the performance of neural networks in a variety of tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What are the conditions for neural networks to be robust to L2-bounded input perturbations? How can we construct neural networks that are robust to L2 perturbations? What is the relationship between L2 robustness and generalization?
the design and analysis of well-conditioned networks that are more robust, more interpretable and more generalizable than ordinary networks.
a new class of well-condition neural networks that can be trained to be robust against white-box Lp-bounded adversarial perturbations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed networks have the potential to become the new state of the art.
this paper proposes neural networks that are robust against adversarial attacks, generalize well from noisy data, have interpretable outputs, and have low Lipschitz constants, all at the same time.
the proposed neural networks are a significant improvement over the state of the practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new class of neural networks, called L2-nonexpansive networks, which are robust against adversarial attacks, generalize better from noisy data, and have meaningful outputs.
the proposed neural networks are more robust and more interpretable than the existing ones.

we have proposed a class of neural networks with a new loss function that can be trained with standard methods and can achieve the state of the arts in robustness, generalization and interpretability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
robustness is not an obstacle to generalization, and that robustness is achievable without sacrificing accuracy on clean data.

the Lipschitz constant of a network is a key quantity to consider when building robust classifiers, and the Lipschitz regularization scheme we propose can be used to build robust and well-behaved networks in general.
robustness is an essential property that can and should be built into the design of neural networks.
